Spacing may be doubled with page margins.
Browser title says goku.ai while the project is named haus-nous.

terms.meaning: A shared wrapper that surrounds every page in the site.
Hidden page information such as the title and description used by browsers and search engines.
A free service that supplies web fonts the browser downloads.
A hint that tells the browser to set up a connection early to speed up loading.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the shared frame
sections.what: Loads the type definition for page metadata, the global style sheet, and the navigation component.
sections.why: Needed for the shared frame to style and navigate every page.
sections.watch_out: The navigation file is outside this packet, so its behavior is unclear here.

sections.name: metadata
sections.title: Browser title and description
sections.what: Sets the title shown in browser tabs and search results to goku.ai, and a short description about shipping strategy pilots.
sections.why: Shows the brand and purpose to visitors and search tools.
sections.watch_out: The name goku.ai differs from the project name, so brand names are mixed across the site.

sections.name: RootLayout
sections.title: Shared page frame
sections.what: Loads fonts from Google, places the navigation at the top, and puts each page's content in the main area. The main area has a left margin on medium screens and wider.
sections.why: Keeps navigation and fonts consistent on every page.
sections.watch_out: Pages add their own large left margin, so spacing may be doubled on wide screens. This cannot be confirmed from this file alone.

summary: The outer frame that every page sits inside: it loads the styles, fonts, the top navigation, and the page title shown in the browser tab.
purpose: Provides the shared structure so each page does not have to repeat the navigation and font loading.
why: Standard Next.js pattern for shared layout. Reason beyond that not stated in the code.
how: Next.js uses this file to wrap every page. It sets the browser title and description, loads the Google fonts, places the navigation, and then puts the current page's content into the main area.
inputs: The page content passed in from each route.
outputs: The full HTML structure of every page.
risks: Layout spacing may overlap with the margins pages add themselves. If the font link fails, text falls back to system fonts.
debug: If the navigation is missing or misplaced, check the Navigation import and the main area's classes. If fonts look wrong, check the font link. Try opening the page with the network tab to see if the font loads.
